title: Make bulk reject and snooze set-based: 50 refs cost 550 SQL statements
body:
## Summary
A bulk reject or snooze of one inbox page (50 cards) runs 550 Forge SQL statements, about 16-33 s at the 30-60 ms per statement store.mjs assumes, so it can pass the 25 s resolver limit and leave a half-decided batch.

## Description
app.mjs:239 checks each ref one by one (openRefs app.mjs:74: findProposal + needInbox per ref), then verdicts.mjs:206 openItems reads each ref again, and verdicts.mjs:226 decideAll runs decide (verdicts.mjs:109: UPDATE, SELECT, appendVerdict SELECT, counter SELECT+UPDATE, INSERT) and cardOf (cards.mjs:118: getInbox + evidenceOf) per card. openItems allows 200 refs (verdicts.mjs:208), i.e. ~2200 statements. The push path was made set-based for exactly this reason (store.mjs:70 "bulk work is a few multi-row statements, not one per row"); the decision path was not. The UI selects many cards and sends them in one call (static/app/src/routes/inbox/useVerdicts.js:81).

## Flow
- person selects a page of cards and presses r
- verdict.reject with 50 refs
- 550 sequential statements
- invocation killed past 25 s: some cards rejected, the UI says the batch is back in the list

## Expected impact
Bulk triage, the inbox's main gesture, stays inside the invocation limit; no half-applied batch the UI misreports.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the call fits Forge's resolver time limit
Before: 550 statements for 50 refs (11 per ref), measured
After: about a dozen statements for 50 refs: one IN read of the refs, one IN read of their inboxes, one CAS UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...) AND status = 'open', one seq block (nextCounterBlock), one multi-row verdict INSERT, one evidenceOfMany
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo ran the real core over forge/test/helpers.mjs countingDb: push 50, then runResolver verdict.reject with the 50 refs -> 550 statements; the After is a design, not built (ideas-only)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "reject50 statements 550 50"; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:208 `if (refs.length > 200) throw ...`; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:229 `for (const p of items) {` -> `cards.push(await cardOf(deps.db, await decide(deps, p, d, who)))`; forge/src/core/app.mjs:74 `if (Array.isArray(refs)) for (const r of refs) if (typeof r === 'string') await acc.proposal(r);`; forge/src/core/store.mjs:70 "Every statement is one Forge SQL request (30-60 ms), so bulk work is a few multi-row statements"
impact_why: bulk reject/snooze of a page is the main triage gesture; past 25 s it half-applies and the UI reports it failed

title: Push areas as sets: 200 areas cost 406 sequential statements
body:
## Summary
dowser_areas_push upserts each area with its own UPDATE and INSERT, so the allowed 200 areas cost 406 statements (12-24 s on Forge SQL), close to the 25 s function limit.

## Description
areas.mjs:72-81 loops over every area: UPDATE, and on 0 rows an INSERT. AREAS_MAX is 200 (types.mjs:33, skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:46). The proposals push next to it is set-based (push.mjs:224 fileAll, store.mjs:102 insertMany); the areas push never got the same treatment. A concurrent INSERT that loses the race also throws an unhandled DuplicateKey (areas.mjs:78), which becomes `unavailable`.

## Flow
- skill runs `areas --top 200` and calls dowser_areas_push
- 200 UPDATE + 200 INSERT on a first push
- call runs 12-24 s; a slow store tips it past the limit

## Expected impact
The map's data push stays well under the time limit at its contract maximum.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - statements per call
Before: 406 statements for 200 areas, measured
After: ~4-6 statements: one IN read of the held paths, one multi-row insertMany of the new ones, UPDATEs only for changed rows (or DELETE then insertMany), one DELETE ... NOT IN
Method: probe - same scratch script, runTool dowser_areas_push with 200 areas on the counting Db -> 406 statements
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "areas200 statements 406 { stored: 200 }"; forge/src/core/areas.mjs:72 `for (const raw of areas) {` / :75 `const u = await db.exec('UPDATE areas SET ...` / :78 `await db.exec('INSERT INTO areas ...`
impact_why: the area push takes half to all of the 25 s budget at its contract cap

title: Store deliveries_json as sets: 500 re-checks cost ~1500 statements
body:
## Summary
dowser_reflect_sync accepts 500 delivery re-checks and stores each with three statements, so a full payload is ~1500 statements (45-90 s), far past the 25 s limit; the sync fails and the skill resends the same payload on every run.

## Description
delivery.mjs:23 DELIVERIES_MAX = 500, mirrored by skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:20, which sends up to 500 (skill reflect.mjs:75 LIMIT ${DELIVERIES_MAX}). delivery.mjs:102-110 runs per entry: SELECT the proposal, ensureRow INSERT (delivery.mjs:58), UPDATE. forge reflect.mjs:90 runs it before the rule offers and the trust are written, so a timeout also drops the rules and trust of that sync.

## Flow
- an inbox with a few hundred accepted cards
- skill reflect sends deliveries_json with up to 500 entries
- 3 statements each, sequential
- the invocation times out; rules, trust and outcomes of that round trip are lost too

## Expected impact
Delivery truth from the code reaches Forge for big inboxes, and a big payload no longer starves the rules/trust sync.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - fits the invocation limit at the contract cap
Before: 156 statements for 50 entries measured (3 per entry + 6), so ~1506 for 500
After: one IN read of the fps, one multi-row insertMany of missing deliveries rows, and chunked updates: under 20 statements for 500
Method: probe - scratch script: 50 accepted cards, runTool dowser_reflect_sync with 50 deliveries on the counting Db -> 156 statements; 500 extrapolated linearly from the per-entry code path
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "reflect_sync 50 deliveries statements 156 ok"; forge/src/core/delivery.mjs:102 `for (const e of ...doc) {` / :103 `SELECT id FROM proposals WHERE project_key = ? AND fp = ? AND status = 'accepted'` / :106 `await ensureRow(...)` / :107 `UPDATE deliveries SET code_state = ?`; skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:20 `export const DELIVERIES_MAX = 500;`
impact_why: a full-size reflect sync cannot finish, taking rules and trust down with it

title: Accept orphans its Jira issue and files a duplicate when the decide step fails
body:
## Summary
Accept creates the Jira issue first, then records the decision. A non-AppError failure of that record step (a Forge SQL error, or the function timing out) is rethrown raw: the caller sees a generic error with no issue key, the claim expires after 2 minutes, and the next accept creates a second issue.

## Description
verdicts.mjs:182 createIssue; verdicts.mjs:191 decide; the catch at verdicts.mjs:194-196 adds the "Jira issue X was created; link or delete it by hand" note only to an AppError and rethrows anything else, which answer() (app.mjs:155-164) turns into "Dowser hit an unexpected error; try again". Nothing records the created key before decide, so after CLAIM_MS (verdicts.mjs:34, 120 s) the claim CAS at verdicts.mjs:168 succeeds again and a retry calls createIssue a second time. The comment at verdicts.mjs:164 says the claim exists so "a double click or a second agent cannot create two issues".

## Flow
- person accepts DW-n
- Jira issue SHOP-41 created
- decide UPDATE hits a transient SQL error, or the invocation is cut
- UI: unexpected error, try again
- two minutes later the retry creates SHOP-42; SHOP-41 has no Dowser record

## Expected impact
One accepted card maps to one Jira issue even across failures; an orphan is either linked or named to the person.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one issue per accept
Before: raw throw after createIssue: no key reported, duplicate on retry after 120 s (re-read of the code)
After: the issue key is stamped on the claimed row before decide (or the catch reports it for every error), and a retry that finds a stamped key finishes the decide instead of calling createIssue
Method: simulation - three cases walked against verdicts.mjs:150-197: AppError from decide (note added, ok), SQL error from decide (raw, no key, retry duplicates), timeout after createIssue (no catch runs, claim expires, retry duplicates); a probe needs a fault-injecting Db not built in an ideas-only round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:194 `} catch (e) {` / :195 `if (e instanceof AppError) throw new AppError(e.code, `${e.message}. Jira issue ${issue.key} was created; link or delete it by hand`);` / :196 `throw e;`; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:168 `UPDATE proposals SET accept_claim = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'open' AND (accept_claim IS NULL OR accept_claim < ?)`
impact_why: duplicate and orphaned Jira issues are visible damage in the customer's tracker

title: Issue-property backfill blocks behind 50 permanently failing rows
body:
## Summary
The daily backfill retries the oldest 50 unwritten issue properties; a write that always fails (issue deleted, moved, or no permission) is never stamped, so 50 such rows block every newer one forever. Without the property, the delivery triggers never fire for those issues.

## Description
issue-property.mjs:87-92 selects `issue_prop_at IS NULL ... ORDER BY decided_at, id LIMIT 50`; writeIssueProperty returns `failed` without stamping (issue-property.mjs:75), so the same rows come back next day. The issue-event trigger filters on the property (manifest.yml dowser-issue-events: `event.runtime.issue.properties['dowser'].ref != null`), so an accepted card whose property never lands gets no delivery truth (delivery.mjs:67). Accepted sample cards whose issues a person later deleted are a ready source of permanent failures.

## Flow
- 50 accepts whose Jira issues were later deleted
- each daily run: the same 50 fail
- a new accept whose write failed transiently is never retried
- its issue gets no delivery events

## Expected impact
Every retryable property write lands within a day; delivery truth covers every accepted card.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - backfill progress
Before: oldest-first LIMIT 50 with no failure mark: head-of-line blocking (re-read)
After: a failure count or last-try stamp (skip after N tries, or order by last attempt) so newer rows advance; a 404 marks the row done
Method: simulation - walked 3 cases through backfillIssueProperties: 0 permanent failures (all advance), 10 (40 newer per day advance), 50 (none advance, ever); not probed because the fake Jira has no per-key failure switch
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/issue-property.mjs:91 `ORDER BY decided_at, id LIMIT ${BACKFILL_MAX}`; forge/src/core/issue-property.mjs:75 `return 'failed';` (no stamp); forge/manifest.yml dowser-issue-events filter `event.runtime.issue.properties['dowser'].ref != null`
impact_why: silently stops the property backfill and delivery truth for every later failed write

title: Page banner asks Jira permissions per inbox on every Confluence page view
body:
## Summary
byline.forPage resolves the caller's visible inboxes (one /mypermissions call per distinct Jira project) before it looks up whether the page has any Dowser link, and the page banner calls it on every page view in the site.

## Description
app.mjs:260 evaluates `await acc.visibleKeys()` as an argument, so access.mjs:87-90 reads every inbox and calls canSee for each before cards.mjs:330 bylineForPage runs its indexed page_links read. The banner module (manifest confluence:pageBanner dowser-doc-banner) renders on every page and calls byline.forPage on mount (static/app/src/routes/byline/Banner.jsx:15). The doc-drift.mjs header says an unlinked page should cost "one indexed lookup".

## Flow
- person opens any Confluence page
- banner calls byline.forPage
- listInboxRows + N Jira permission requests
- page_links answers zero rows; banner renders nothing

## Expected impact
An unlinked page view costs one indexed read and no Jira calls; fewer GB-seconds and no Jira rate-limit pressure from browsing Confluence.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - Jira requests per unlinked page view
Before: 20 permission calls and 3 statements on a site with 20 inboxes, measured
After: 1 statement and 0 permission calls: read page_links first and return early when empty, then check access only for the inboxes the links name
Method: probe - scratch script: 20 inboxes each bound to its own Jira project, runResolver byline.forPage on an unlinked page with the fake Perms port counting calls
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "byline unlinked page: statements 3 perm calls 20 0"; forge/src/core/app.mjs:260 `'byline.forPage': async (d, p, _, __, acc) => bylineForPage(d.db, needStr(p, 'page_id'), await acc.visibleKeys()),`; forge/src/core/access.mjs:89 `const ok = await Promise.all(rows.map((r) => canSee(r)));`
impact_why: every Confluence page view on the site pays N Jira calls for a banner that is almost always empty

title: Page event with an unparseable version date throws instead of being dropped
body:
## Summary
onPageEvent promises "Never throws for a bad event", but a linked page whose event carries a non-ISO version.when throws RangeError, so the edit is not recorded.

## Description
doc-drift.mjs:99 does `new Date(Date.parse(event.content.version.when)).toISOString()` whenever `when` is a string; Date.parse answers NaN for a bad string and toISOString throws RangeError. The doc at doc-drift.mjs:89 says it never throws; the entry point catches and logs (index.js:153-157), so the only trace is a "page event failed" line and the byline loses its page_edited_since_decision flag for that edit.

## Flow
- Confluence sends avi:confluence:updated:page for a linked page
- version.when is a string Date.parse cannot read
- RangeError: Invalid time value
- no page_edits row

## Expected impact
A malformed date falls back to deps.now(), as the absent case already does; the contract in the comment holds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - documented contract holds
Before: throws RangeError (probe)
After: Number.isNaN(Date.parse(when)) falls back to now(); no throw
Method: probe - scratch script: push a record with doc_impact ["777"], then onPageEvent({content:{id:"777",version:{when:"not a date"}}}) -> "onPageEvent threw RangeError Invalid time value"
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "onPageEvent threw RangeError Invalid time value"; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:99 `const when = typeof event?.content?.version?.when === 'string' ? new Date(Date.parse(event.content.version.when)).toISOString() : deps.now().toISOString();`; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:89 "Never throws for a bad event."
impact_why: rare malformed events lose one edit stamp; contract mismatch

title: Give dowser_work_list a cursor: items past the oldest 50 are unreachable
body:
## Summary
work_list answers the oldest 50 accepted items and `more: true`, but takes no cursor, so the 51st and later work items can never be listed; it also reads every accepted row and every work report of the inbox on each call.

## Description
work.mjs:45-46 reads all accepted proposals with no LIMIT; work.mjs:30-33 reads every work_reports row of all of them; work.mjs:62 returns the first 50 with `more: true`. The contract (docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md:443-446) documents `{items, more?}` with no cursor input. `open` leaves out only Jira-delivered or abandoned items, so 50 old accepted items not delivered in Jira (stale, or delivered only in the code) hide every newer one from the agent. The IN lists (work.mjs:32, delivery.mjs:135) grow with the inbox and are not chunked like store.mjs inChunks.

## Flow
- inbox with 80 accepted, undelivered items
- agent calls dowser_work_list queue open
- gets the oldest 50 and more: true
- no input reaches item 51

## Expected impact
An agent can page the whole work queue; each call reads one page, not the inbox.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the agent can reach all accepted work
Before: items beyond 50 unreachable (re-read of code and contract)
After: an `after` cursor (last decided_at, id) and LIMIT 51 in SQL; reports read for the page only
Method: simulation - walked 3 cases: 30 items (all listed), 50 (all, no more), 80 (30 unreachable by any call); the contract offers no cursor field
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: forge/src/core/work.mjs:46 `"SELECT * FROM proposals WHERE project_key = ? AND status = 'accepted' ORDER BY decided_at, id", [projectKey]`; forge/src/core/work.mjs:62 `return items.length > WORK_PAGE ? { items: items.slice(0, WORK_PAGE), more: true } : { items };`; docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md:444 "Output `{items, more?}`: at most 50, oldest decision first"
impact_why: past 50 accepted items the agent work queue silently stops reaching new work

title: Share the wire caps: PUSH/AREAS/RULES/DELIVERIES/DIRECTION limits are hand-copied
body:
## Summary
The contract caps live twice, in forge/src/core (types.mjs, delivery.mjs) and again in skill/scripts/lib (sync.mjs, reflect.mjs, direction.mjs), while sync-shared copies only model.mjs and fingerprint.mjs; no test pins the copies equal.

## Description
forge/scripts/sync-shared.mjs:18 SHARED = [model.mjs, fingerprint.mjs]. Duplicated pairs: PUSH_MAX (types.mjs:25 / sync.mjs:43), AREAS_MAX (types.mjs:33 / sync.mjs:46), RULES_MAX and TRUST_EVENTS_MAX (types.mjs / skill reflect.mjs:22,25), DELIVERIES_MAX (delivery.mjs:23 / skill reflect.mjs:20), DIRECTION_ITEMS_MAX, DIRECTION_LINE_MAX, DIRECTION_SPACES_MAX, SPACE_KEY_RE (types.mjs:35-39 / skill direction.mjs:22-26). The skill comments name the Forge file as the source ("forge/src/core/delivery.mjs DELIVERIES_MAX"): the mirror is a promise, not a check. forge/test/shared.test.mjs pins only the two copied files. Lowering a Forge cap (e.g. for the time-limit findings in this round) without the skill side makes every full-size call `bad-input`.

## Flow
- Forge lowers DELIVERIES_MAX to fit the time limit
- skill still sends 500
- every reflect sync from an inbox with more accepted cards than the cap is refused

## Expected impact
One source for the wire caps; a drift fails a test, not a customer's sync.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source of truth for contract caps
Before: 9 caps defined on both sides, 0 tests comparing them (grep)
After: the caps move into model.mjs (already byte-synced) and both sides import them, or a test asserts each pair equal
Method: gate - grep for the constants across forge/ and skill/: no file outside the two libs references them; shared.test.mjs covers only SHARED
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/scripts/sync-shared.mjs:18 `export const SHARED = ['model.mjs', 'fingerprint.mjs'];`; forge/src/core/types.mjs:25 `export const PUSH_MAX = 50;` vs skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:43 `export const PUSH_MAX = 50;`; forge/src/core/types.mjs:35 `export const DIRECTION_ITEMS_MAX = 10;` vs skill/scripts/lib/direction.mjs:22; skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:19 "(forge/src/core/delivery.mjs DELIVERIES_MAX)"; grep DIRECTION_ITEMS_MAX|DELIVERIES_MAX|SPACE_KEY_RE outside the libs: no hits
impact_why: the next cap change on one side silently breaks the other side's full-size calls

title: Raw SQL and Jira error text is logged and returned despite the no-internals rule
body:
## Summary
answer() logs an unexpected error by name and code only because "an error's message can carry Jira response text or SQL detail", but ten other sites put the raw message into a log line or into the AppError text sent to the caller.

## Description
Rule: app.mjs:149-151 and observe.mjs:6 ("never the error message ... Never a payload body, a note, a message"). Breaks: verdicts.mjs:131 logs the SQL error of appendVerdict; issue-property.mjs:74, names.mjs:27 and reflect.mjs:328 log Jira messages; verdicts.mjs:188 and :308, work.mjs:120, doc-drift.mjs:166, sources.mjs:91 and app.mjs:248 return `(${e.message})` to the UI or agent. The Jira adapter errors carry response text (adapters/atlassian.mjs json()).

## Flow
- Jira answers 400 with a body naming fields, or Forge SQL fails with statement detail
- message embedded in an AppError or a log line
- shown in the UI, handed to the agent, kept in Forge logs

## Expected impact
One redaction rule for every error path; logs keep codes and statuses, not bodies.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated logging and leak policy holds everywhere
Before: 10 sites embed raw messages (grep)
After: a shared errTag(e) (name, code, HTTP status) used at every site; the person-facing text names the system and status only
Method: gate - grep "(e).message" and "message: String(" across forge/src/core; each hit re-read
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/app.mjs:150 "anything else is logged by its name and code only (an error's message can carry Jira response text or SQL detail)"; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:131 `console.warn(`dowser: verdict for ${p.ref} not logged yet (${/** @type {Error} */ (e).message}); the next pull repairs it`);`; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:188 `throw new AppError('unavailable', `Jira did not create the issue (${... (e).message}); ${p.ref} stays open`);`; forge/src/core/issue-property.mjs:74 `message: String(... (e)?.message ?? e).slice(0, 200)`
impact_why: policy pair broken in ten places; Jira bodies and SQL detail reach logs and callers

title: An abandoned issue flips to delivered on its next done-to-done transition
body:
## Summary
jiraStateOf decides abandoned vs delivered only from a resolution change in the event changelog, so a later status move inside the done category (Resolved -> Closed) with the resolution unchanged records a Won't Do issue as delivered.

## Description
delivery.mjs:36-38 reads `changelog.items.find(field === 'resolution')`; without such an item the state is `delivered`. The trigger fires on any status change (manifest dowser-issue-events filter `i.field == 'status' || i.field == 'resolution'`), and onIssueEvent overwrites jira_state (delivery.mjs:75). Candidates then show done: true and the outcome prompt treats abandoned work as delivered (forge reflect.mjs:336).

## Flow
- issue resolved Won't Do: event records abandoned
- workflow later moves it Resolved -> Closed (both done), no resolution item
- event records delivered
- Learning tab asks how the delivered work turned out

## Expected impact
Delivery truth keeps abandoned work abandoned; outcome prompts stay honest.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - delivery state is correct
Before: state depends on whether this event changed the resolution (re-read)
After: read the current resolution from event.issue.fields.resolution when present, else keep a stored abandoned state on a done-to-done move
Method: simulation - walked 3 events: Won't Do resolve (abandoned, right), Done resolve (delivered, right), Closed move after Won't Do (delivered, wrong); whether the Forge event carries fields.resolution was not verified
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/delivery.mjs:36 `if (cat === 'done') {` / :37 `const res = (event?.changelog?.items ?? []).find((i) => i?.field === 'resolution')?.toString;` / :38 `return { state: typeof res === 'string' && ABANDONED_RESOLUTIONS.has(res.toLowerCase()) ? 'abandoned' : 'delivered', status };`
impact_why: abandoned work counted as delivered skews the Learning tab and outcome prompts

title: Proposal lookups answer before the access check, leaking existence across inboxes
body:
## Summary
acc.proposal runs findProposal first, so a caller who may not open an inbox learns from the error whether a DW ref exists and whether a fingerprint also sits in another inbox.

## Description
access.mjs:82-85 calls findProposal (store.mjs:335) and only then the inbox check. store.mjs:342 answers `no Dowser proposal X` (bad-input) for a missing ref but `forbidden` for one that exists; store.mjs:343 answers "fingerprint X is in more than one inbox" when another, invisible inbox holds the same finding (the same repo scanned by another team). The access module promises the denial "names what would open it, never its content" (access.mjs:26).

## Flow
- caller without access sends proposal.get DW-1..DW-n
- bad-input vs forbidden tells which exist
- an fp lookup reveals that another inbox holds the same finding

## Expected impact
An unopenable inbox reveals nothing, not even existence.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - access denial leaks nothing
Before: two distinguishable answers (re-read)
After: fp lookups filtered to visible inboxes before the ambiguity check; a missing and a forbidden ref answer the same
Method: simulation - walked: ref missing (bad-input), ref in a hidden inbox (forbidden), fp in a hidden and a visible inbox (ambiguity error on the visible one); low stakes: refs are sequential and fps carry no content
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/access.mjs:83 `const p = await findProposal(deps.db, ref);` / :84 `await inbox(p.project_key);`; forge/src/core/store.mjs:342 `if (rows.length === 0) throw new AppError('bad-input', `no Dowser proposal ${r}`);` / :343 `fingerprint ${r} is in more than one inbox; use its DW ref`
impact_why: existence-only leak; refs are sequential and fps carry no content

title: A second person on the site cannot try the sample and is told it was "pushed"
body:
## Summary
The sample inbox is open only to the person who loaded it (and Jira admins), so a teammate sees the first-run screen, presses Load the sample, and gets forbidden with copy about "the person who first pushed to it".

## Description
sample.mjs:116 opens an existing sample through the inbox access rule; the sample has no Jira project, so access.mjs:65 admits only `created_by`. A non-admin second user has no visible inbox, so the inbox shows FirstRun (static/app/src/routes/inbox/index.jsx:146), whose button calls sample.load (FirstRun.jsx:22) and shows the error. denied() (access.mjs:32) says "only the person who first pushed to it and Jira admins can open it" - nobody pushed the sample. setup.status reports `sample.loaded: true` to everyone (sample.mjs:190) without checking access.

## Flow
- evaluator A loads the sample
- evaluator B opens Dowser: first-run screen
- B presses Load the sample
- B reads "You cannot open the Dowser inbox dowser-sample; ... only the person who first pushed to it"

## Expected impact
Every person on a site can try the sample (it is a public repo's scan), or is at least told who loaded it and how to get access.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a second evaluator reaches the sample
Before: forbidden dead end with push wording (re-read)
After: the sample inbox is readable by anyone with the app, or the denial for SAMPLE_KEY names the loader and the Settings step
Method: simulation - walked three users: the loader (opens), a Jira admin (opens), a plain user (forbidden at sample.mjs:116); not probed in the UI
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: forge/src/core/sample.mjs:116 `if (inbox) await accessFor(deps, accountId).inbox(SAMPLE_KEY);`; forge/src/core/access.mjs:65 `} else if (inbox.created_by === me) {`; forge/src/core/access.mjs:32 `'until a Jira project is set for it in Dowser settings, only the person who first pushed to it and Jira admins can open it'`
impact_why: the sample is the evaluator first run; a second evaluator on the site hits a dead end

title: Inbox summaries read the newest push once per inbox
body:
## Summary
inboxSummaries runs one pushes query per visible inbox and a GROUP BY over every proposal of every inbox, on every inbox.list, settings.get and Rovo list call.

## Description
cards.mjs:167 counts proposals of all inboxes (no project filter, so the work grows with inboxes the caller cannot see); cards.mjs:176 queries pushes once per inbox inside the loop. listInbox calls it on every page (cards.mjs:259), so each scroll page costs N+1 extra statements.

## Flow
- site with 20 inboxes
- every inbox page or settings view
- 20 pushes queries plus a full-table GROUP BY

## Expected impact
Summaries cost two statements whatever the inbox count.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - statements per inbox.list
Before: 1 + N statements for N visible inboxes (re-read)
After: one GROUP BY restricted to the visible keys and one pushes read with IN (...) keeping the newest per inbox in memory
Method: simulation - walked N = 1, 5, 20 through inboxSummaries: 2, 6, 21 statements; at 30-60 ms each, 20 inboxes add ~1 s per page
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/cards.mjs:167 `SELECT project_key, status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM proposals GROUP BY project_key, status`; forge/src/core/cards.mjs:176 `const push = (await db.query('SELECT * FROM pushes WHERE project_key = ? ORDER BY at DESC, id LIMIT 1', [i.project_key]))[0];`
impact_why: adds about 1 s per inbox page on a 20-inbox site

title: Make the page-link backfill resumable instead of restarting from id 0
body:
## Summary
backfillPageLinks walks every proposal in one invocation and marks itself done only at the end, so a run cut by the time limit starts again from id 0 the next day and may never finish on a large site.

## Description
doc-drift.mjs:77 loops from after = 0 over all proposals in pages of 200, with one INSERT per page id (doc-drift.mjs:43 linkPages); the done mark is written only after the loop (doc-drift.mjs:84). It runs after the issue-property backfill inside the same daily migrate invocation (index.js:185-188), with no timeoutSeconds in forge/manifest.yml. No progress cursor is stored, unlike sample.mjs's budgeted, resumable load.

## Flow
- site upgraded with thousands of older proposals
- daily migrate: migrations, property backfill, page backfill
- invocation ends before the loop does
- next day starts again at id 0

## Expected impact
Older items get their byline and banner links within a few days on any site size.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the backfill completes
Before: all-or-nothing loop, progress lost on timeout (re-read)
After: store the last id after each page and stop past a time budget, as loadSample does
Method: simulation - walked 3 sizes: 500 proposals (one run), 5000 with few links (likely one run), 5000 with several page ids each (one INSERT per link, can exceed the budget and repeat daily)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:77 `for (let after = 0; ;) {`; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:84 `await nextCounter(deps.db, BACKFILL_COUNTER);` (after the loop only)
impact_why: large sites may never get page links for pre-v030 items
